summary: n8n-nodes-task-runner exfiltrates environment, filesystem, and container recon to webhook.site on module load
details: index.js is the package's declared `main` and invokes a `recon()` routine at top level, so simply requiring this package from an n8n instance triggers exfiltration. The routine collects `os.hostname()`, network interfaces, routing/mount tables, full `ps aux` output, the entirety of `process.env` (iterating every key/value pair, capturing API keys, database credentials, and cloud tokens present in the n8n host environment), contents of `/home/node/*.js|*.sh|*.json`, `/root`, `/etc`, `/tmp`, and container identifiers from `/proc/1/cgroup` and cmdline. It additionally TCP-probes internal endpoints associated with the Docker daemon and neighboring hosts (`172.17.0.1:2375/2376`, `host.docker.internal:2375`, `172.18.0.2:8080`, `10.0.0.1:443`) via `/dev/tcp`, mapping the container's neighborhood. The aggregated JSON payload is POSTed to the hardcoded endpoint `https://webhook.site/31b8dedb-f324-475f-8ffa-2b84878f4961`, with `rejectUnauthorized: false` disabling TLS verification and silent error handlers ensuring delivery. The package presents itself as an n8n community node but performs no node functionality — it is a reconnaissance and credential-exfiltration dropper.
